Is a value inside a range?

Source: R/phrases.R
in_range.Rd

in_range(x, range) is TRUE where range[1] <= x and x <= range[2], element by element, and NA where x is NA. The bounds are inside the range. range is a range entry of the dictionary, as in in_range(do_mean, dict$do_band), or any two numbers in order.

Usage

in_range(x, range)

Arguments

x

A number or a quantity (a units value, see u()).

range

Two numbers, lower first; a units pair for a quantity.

Value

A logical vector the length of x.

Details

A quantity x is converted to the unit of the range. Units that do not convert, a number against a range with a unit (or the reverse), and a range that is not two numbers with the lower below the upper are a weft_value_error. It is an R function: the filter has no dictionary, so it is written in a governor's if where R evaluates it.

Examples

in_range(c(6, 7, 9), c(6.5, 8.5))
#> [1] FALSE  TRUE FALSE
